title: Void Seekers and Celestial Masters
summary: The two roots of the Void Engineers.

claims.text: The earliest Seekers of the Void were wanderers in every culture who valued fellowship above origin or creed and met strange beasts and spirits at the world's edges.
Those who stayed in the growing cities became the Celestial Masters, charting the skies and advising rulers.
Swapping knowledge over a few centuries, the two groups formed the partnership that became the Convention.

title: Void Engineer Marines
summary: The militarised Convention after the Anomaly.

claims.text: In the Anomaly's early days whole amalgams, ships and Constructs were lost, so the Convention expanded its security arms and militarised many co-ops.
Everyone in the Convention now gets full combat training, down to the cleaning staff.
The Marines once played up a Terminator image as a joke; now they lead boarding actions on space hulks and assaults on enemy holds in earnest.
The BCD hunts threats in the Near Universe before they cross the Gauntlet: Nephandi, Marauders, alien minds and spirits maddened by the Anomaly.
Nearly all its Marines also trained at a Void Engineer college and are scientists as well as fighters.
They serve as a model for post-Anomaly Technocrats, the Progenitors' Applied Sciences above all.
The EFD maps remote wilds and buried urban places such as old sewers and ruins under ice and sand.
It also explores legendary sites such as Fiddler's Green, Ker-Ys in Brittany and lost Mu with its imitators.
It claims the Seekers as ancestors, people in every culture unwilling to spend their lives in one place.

title: Neutralization Specialist Corps
summary: The Convention's second line of defence on Earth.

claims.text: The NSC steps in when threats from beyond slip past the Convention's thinned defences and reach Earth.
Its outlook echoes an early goal of the Order of Reason: stopping mages who traded with alien powers for knowledge and opened doors for them.
The PDC goes past the Spatial Horizon into the Deep Universe and sets up beachheads across the galaxy.
Its prehistory starts with the Seeker Tychoides, who led early trips through the Gauntlet and found the Universe harsh and unforgiving.
It was formed at the Grand Housecleaning to explore beyond a Horizon that then reached little past the Moon and to build Constructs nearby.

title: Research & Execution
summary: The Void Engineers who keep the home fires burning.

claims.text: R&E repairs gear and vessels and runs labs; 32.7% of its people stay home, down from about 55% before 1999.
The rest serve in the field as ship engineers, Device specialists and researchers.
Its roots lie with the Celestial Masters, who drew the first star charts and, ironically, horoscopes.

title: The Dimensional Anomaly
summary: The Avatar Storm as the Void Engineers lived it.

claims.text: The Anomaly struck at the end of June 1999, tearing across the Spatial Horizon like a hurricane with reality at its eye.
It began to ease by New Year's Day 2000 and lessened again by autumn 2000, yet it never fully ended.
Everett Volumes, named for the man who founded the Many Worlds idea, cross dimensions and hold other timelines, such as one where Technocrats fight a Tradition tyranny.
